summary: French colonies, protectorates and mandated territories formed through distinct waves of overseas expansion, with different systems of administration and citizenship.
capital: Paris; Versailles was the principal royal seat of government from 1682 to 1789, with interruptions.
currency: Currencies varied across territories; the CFA and CFP francs were created in 1945 within the colonial monetary system.
rulers: Selected monarch: Louis XIV, 1643–1715. Later colonial rule continued under other monarchies and republics.
economy: Caribbean plantation exports relied on enslaved labor; other territories supplied commodities and trading bases under changing colonial economic arrangements.
military: French armed forces conducted colonial conquests, including Algeria from 1830 and extensive African campaigns during the late nineteenth century.
contributions: Colonial encounters produced enduring cultural and linguistic exchanges while imposed rule and slavery reshaped colonized societies.
origin: Commercial ventures, strategic rivalry and missionary objectives developed into state-directed overseas colonization.
decline: Wars, independence movements and decolonization dismantled most imperial rule; Vanuatu’s independence ended the Anglo-French condominium in 1980.
periodNote: 1534 marks Cartier’s first voyage; 1980 marks Vanuatu’s independence, not the disappearance of French overseas territories. First and second colonial empires are often studied separately.
